abstract: Can a dense grid set be doubled while retaining local ancestry and selected geometric constraints? For every fixed finite set of primitive normals $D$ containing the axes, every fixed parent distance $L$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that any $D$-capped set $P$ in a side-$n$ square has at least $2|P|-\varepsilon n-o(n)$ labelled children in the exact side-$2n$ square. Each retained parent has two children within $O(n^{9/10})$ of twice its position. The output has line caps two in $D$, pair separation greater than $n^{1/5}/2$, and no collinear triple containing children of a parent pair at distance at most $L$, including siblings and a distant third parent. Canonical parabola packets remove any no-three assumption on the input. Random integer affine distortion, an exact projection-kernel estimate, sparse conflict removal, and common-pool padding verify the hypotheses of a classical fixed-rank matching theorem. A slow diagonal choice gives loss $o(n)$ and some $L(n)\to\infty$. Separately, for genuine no-three parents and any $L=o(n^{2/3})$, piecewise cyclic translations give local parent and child triple protection with loss and displacement $O(\max\{n^{2/3},\sqrt n L^{3/4}\})$. An elementary convex-order condition explains rigidity under fixed midpoints. Complete proofs and four exact interface controllers are supplied. Three mutually distant packets remain uncontrolled; the results give neither a full no-three recurrence nor an asymptotic density improvement.
